title: Thread and Matter: IPv6 mesh, Border Router, and commissioning

spans.text: Thread is a low-power IPv6 mesh network. Matter is an application-layer standard for interoperable home devices; Thread is one network it can use.

Thread routes IPv6/6LoWPAN packets over IEEE 802.15.4. Routers forward traffic; a Sleepy End Device can sleep to save battery; a Border Router routes IP packets between Thread and the wider IP network, but does not itself translate the application protocol. OpenThread can run as a standalone node on 802.15.4 chips such as ESP32-H2/C6, or use an RCP over UART/SPI with a separate host.

Matter defines an application model and secure commissioning; it can run over Wi-Fi, Ethernet, or Thread. A Matter-over-Thread device needs a Thread Border Router and a Matter controller. Thread and Zigbee both use 802.15.4 but have different network and application protocols and are not interchangeable. ESP-IDF's `ot_cli` example forms a Thread network with two boards; Matter development separately uses ESP-Matter and a supported target.
Build the ESP-IDF OpenThread CLI example

spans.code:
idf.py set-target esp32h2
idf.py menuconfig
idf.py -p PORT build flash monitor

# On node 1, form the network and copy the active dataset hex:
ot dataset init new
ot dataset commit active
ot ifconfig up
ot thread start
ot dataset active -x

# On node 2, replace the placeholder with node 1's dataset hex:
ot dataset set active ACTIVE_DATASET_HEX
ot ifconfig up
ot thread start
ot state

spans.text: Add the Matter SDK to an ESP-IDF project

spans.code:
idf.py add-dependency "espressif/esp_matter^1.4.0"

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: OpenThread and Matter support depends on ESP-IDF/ESP-Matter versions and radio capabilities. Thread and Zigbee devices do not join the same network directly. Protect commissioning credentials and setup codes.
